# Preface {.unnumbered}

These notes are a self-study of the book ***Emmy Noether's Wonderful Theorem*** by Dwight E. Neuenschwander. They contain my main summaries from each chapter, together with my solutions to some of his exercises and a few discussions of my own along the way.

The book builds up to Noether's theorem, the statement that every continuous symmetry of a physical theory comes with a conserved quantity, and then explores its consequences in mechanics and field theory.

## Chapters

**Chapter 1 — Introduction to Symmetries**
: What a symmetry is · Galilean and Poincaré invariance · A first link between translation symmetry and momentum conservation · Invariance versus conservation · Covariance

**Chapter 2 — Functionals**
: Functionals as maps from paths to numbers · The action and the Lagrangian · Fermat's principle · Exercises on path-dependent functionals and Hamilton's principle

More chapters will be added as I read on.

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| $\mathbf r,\ \mathbf p$ | Position and momentum vectors |
| $\dot q = dq/dt$ | Time derivative |
| $q^\mu(t),\ \mu = 1,\ldots,N$ | Generalized coordinates |
| $L(q^\mu, \dot q^\mu, t)$ | Lagrangian |
| $S[q^\mu]$ | Action functional, with square brackets for the argument of a functional |
| $C^2([a,b], \mathbb R^N)$ | Twice continuously differentiable paths $[a,b] \to \mathbb R^N$ |
